title: Heavy Metal Tested & Certified — published standards
description: The HMTc certification limits per product subcategory, variant, and analyte: the published limit in ppb on the row's native basis, the control basis (government-limit default, government read-across, or controlled screen), the controlling jurisdiction and instrument, and — for government-limit cells — the per-country table of sovereign limits the value was selected from. Values are set by Method v2.0 (strictest applicable government maximum level, selective occurrence for Tier-1 toxics and unregulated cells).
methodology_version: HMTc-10 / Method v2.0 — government-limit default, selective occurrence for Tier-1 toxics and unregulated cells (CLAUDE.md Part 19)

license.terms: The published HMTc standards are free to read and cite with attribution. The derivation methodology and this compiled dataset are the work of Paleo Certified, Inc., operating as the Institute of Contaminant Standards.
license.attribution: Heavy Metal Tested & Certified (HMTc), Institute of Contaminant Standards. Cite the standard's page_url and standard_version.

evidence_basis: Literature occurrence evidence the standards are checked against is reported independently at https://heavymetalindex.com and cited one-way; see each record's hmi_literature_link.

Mandatory total-As cell; iAs cannot satisfy the total-As requirement (iAs <= tAs). Applied as a government read-across for this juice matrix, which India's infant-foods scope does not name directly.

standards.name: Baby lotion and cream
standards.native_basis: finished cosmetic product as placed on the market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, never a migration or leachate number, never a colour-additive or raw-material purity specification, and never a dietary basis.
standards.methodology_version: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default) as applied to a child-scoped cosmetic category: every numeric cell is the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic maximum in the row's native total-content basis, or a disclosed read-across of a stricter sovereign tier from the same instrument where that instrument writes an adult-market loosening carve-out that HMTc declines to adopt for a product marketed to ages 0-5. No cell is occurrence-derived.

all.native_basis: finished cosmetic product as placed on the market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, never a migration or leachate number, never a colour-additive or raw-material purity specification, and never a dietary basis.

Pb.native_basis: finished cosmetic product as placed on the market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, never a migration or leachate number, never a colour-additive or raw-material purity specification, and never a dietary basis.
Pb.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

Cd.native_basis: finished cosmetic product as placed on the market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, never a migration or leachate number, never a colour-additive or raw-material purity specification, and never a dietary basis.
Cd.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

standards.name: Vegetable juices, non-root
standards.methodology_version: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.rationale: No credible sovereign has written a lead maximum level for vegetable juice: EU 2023/915 section 3.1.19, Codex CXS 193 and Hong Kong Cap 132V all scope their juice lead cells to FRUIT juices and nectars. The nearest applicable sovereign value is therefore the EU fruit-juice lead cell (30 ug/kg) in the identical single-strength ready-to-drink basis, and it is adopted by disclosed read-across.

Cd.rationale: No credible sovereign has written a cadmium maximum level for vegetable juice, so the cell is anchored on the strictest applicable sovereign cadmium cell across the vegetable families this row covers. The Hong Kong Cap 132V fruiting-vegetable cells (50 ug/kg) bind; the general vegetable cell that covers tomatoes (100 ug/kg) and the EU leaf-vegetable cell (100 ug/kg) are disclosed and not adopted.

tAs.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign has written an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for vegetable juice. The nearest applicable sovereign value is the EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit-juice cell (20 ug/kg) in the identical single-strength ready-to-drink basis, adopted by disclosed read-across.

tHg.rationale: No credible sovereign has written a total-mercury maximum level for vegetable juice itself, but Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 12 sets mercury, expressed as total mercury, in vegetables other than edible fungi at 10 ug/kg, and that is the source-commodity cell for a non-root vegetable juice. It is adopted by disclosed read-across from the same instrument and on the same logic as this row's cadmium anchor: mercury reaches a vegetable juice through the vegetable, so the source-commodity cell is the nearest applicable sovereign value.

MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.

Al.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

Cr.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

Cr-VI.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium is not a routine lot test. Pb.basis_note: child-protective read-across (voluntary over-compliance; adult floor disclosed, never selected)
Pb.rationale: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food lead maximum (AU-NZ infant formula, 10 µg/kg). Adult supplement floors run 1000-10000 µg/kg (Thailand 1000; GSO/Israel/Vietnam 3000; ASEAN/Singapore 10000) and adult USP <2232> permits 5 µg/day (500 µg/kg at 10 g/day); California's developmental lead MADL is 0.5 µg/day. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 10 µg/kg because children consume adult supplements and lead has no threshold.

iAs.basis_note: child-protective read-across (voluntary over-compliance; adult floor disclosed, never selected)
iAs.rationale: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food inorganic-arsenic maximum (EU infant formula, 10 µg/kg). No government sets an inorganic-arsenic supplement ML; adult USP <2232> permits inorganic arsenic 15 µg/day (1500 µg/kg at 10 g/day). HMTc holds ALL supplements to 10 µg/kg inorganic arsenic — 150x below the adult USP concentration floor. Basis disclosure: this EU anchor (source_id eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10) is set on a liquid, as-consumed basis and is read across to the as-sold solid supplement WITHOUT a reconstitution adjustment. A reconstituted liquid formula is roughly 6-8x more dilute than the equivalent as-sold powder, so applying the liquid value directly to a solid is an intentional, disclosed over-strictness (the solid cell runs ~6-8x stricter than the equivalent as-sold powder ML), never an accidental wet/dry conflation; no serving-size conversion selects the limit.

tAs.basis_note: child-protective read-across (voluntary over-compliance; adult floor disclosed, never selected)
tAs.rationale: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food total-arsenic maximum (India infant foods, 50 µg/kg). Total arsenic gates the inorganic-arsenic reflex; the toxic species iAs is anchored separately at 10 µg/kg. Adult supplement floors run 300-5000 µg/kg. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 50 µg/kg total arsenic.

Pb.rationale: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food lead maximum (AU-NZ infant formula, 10 µg/kg). Adult supplement floors run 1000-10000 µg/kg (Thailand 1000; GSO/Israel/Vietnam 3000; ASEAN/Singapore 10000) and adult USP <2232> permits 5 µg/day (500 µg/kg at 10 g/day); California's developmental lead MADL is 0.5 µg/day. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 10 µg/kg because children consume adult supplements and lead has no threshold.

iAs.basis_note: child-protective read-across (voluntary over-compliance; adult floor disclosed, never selected)
iAs.rationale: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food inorganic-arsenic maximum (EU infant formula, 10 µg/kg). No government sets an inorganic-arsenic supplement ML; adult USP <2232> permits inorganic arsenic 15 µg/day (1500 µg/kg at 10 g/day). HMTc holds ALL supplements to 10 µg/kg inorganic arsenic — 150x below the adult USP concentration floor. Basis disclosure: this EU anchor (source_id eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10) is set on a liquid, as-consumed basis and is read across to the as-sold solid supplement WITHOUT a reconstitution adjustment. A reconstituted liquid formula is roughly 6-8x more dilute than the equivalent as-sold powder, so applying the liquid value directly to a solid is an intentional, disclosed over-strictness (the solid cell runs ~6-8x stricter than the equivalent as-sold powder ML), never an accidental wet/dry conflation; no serving-size conversion selects the limit.

tAs.basis_note: child-protective read-across (voluntary over-compliance; adult floor disclosed, never selected)
tAs.rationale: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food total-arsenic maximum (India infant foods, 50 µg/kg). Total arsenic gates the inorganic-arsenic reflex; the toxic species iAs is anchored separately at 10 µg/kg. Adult supplement floors run 300-5000 µg/kg. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 50 µg/kg total arsenic.

Species never replace totals, no ingredient purity specification anchors a finished-product cell, no migration value anchors a content cell, and no cell is occurrence-derived.

all.native_basis: finished denture or appliance care product as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)

Pb.native_basis: finished denture or appliance care product as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
Pb.rationale: The exact cell is unregulated: no sovereign publishes a lead value for this product form. Germany BVL 2017's toothpaste tier (0.5 mg/kg) is the nearest applicable sovereign cell because it is the only sovereign lead value written for a product applied to the oral mucosa and partly swallowed, which is this form's exposure pattern. The directly applicable German general-cosmetic tier is 2 mg/kg; HMTc reads the stricter oral tier across rather than taking the looser general value, and discloses that choice here rather than presenting the number as direct regulatory alignment.

Cd.native_basis: finished denture or appliance care product as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
Cd.rationale: The row spans a cosmetic sub-form (intraoral adhesive) and a non-cosmetic sub-form (appliance soak cleanser), so no sovereign instrument directly regulates the whole row. The Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier is read across as the nearest applicable sovereign cell for a product whose residue reaches the oral mucosa; it is equal to the strictest general-cosmetic value for this analyte, so the read-across neither tightens nor loosens the number relative to the cosmetic instrument family.

tHg.native_basis: finished denture or appliance care product as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
tHg.rationale: The row spans a cosmetic sub-form (intraoral adhesive) and a non-cosmetic sub-form (appliance soak cleanser), so no sovereign instrument directly regulates the whole row. The Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier is read across as the nearest applicable sovereign cell for a product whose residue reaches the oral mucosa; it is equal to the strictest general-cosmetic value for this analyte, so the read-across neither tightens nor loosens the number relative to the cosmetic instrument family.

MeHg.native_basis: finished denture or appliance care product as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold or CV-AAS. No separate methylmercury determination is required for an oral-care matrix; any lot above 50% of the total-mercury ceiling is investigated to its mercury source before release.

Ni.native_basis: finished denture or appliance care product as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
Ni.rationale: No sovereign names nickel in an oral-care product. Korea MFDS is the only jurisdiction in the register that sets a finished-cosmetic nickel content limit at all, and it tiers it by product type: eye makeup 35 ug/g, colour makeup 30 ug/g, and all other cosmetic products 10 ug/g. An oral-care product is neither eye makeup nor a colour cosmetic, so the residual 'other products' tier — the STRICTEST of the three — is the nearest applicable sovereign cell and is read across. The named anchor is MFDS Notice No. 2025-63 (Cosmetics Safety Standards), the current Korean instrument. HMTc does not use the looser makeup tiers.

An oral-care product is neither eye makeup nor a colour cosmetic, so the residual 'other products' tier — the STRICTEST of the three — is the nearest applicable sovereign cell and is read across. The named anchor is MFDS Notice No. 2025-63 (Cosmetics Safety Standards), the current Korean instrument. HMTc does not use the looser makeup tiers.

standards.name: Cheese
standards.methodology_version: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; no dairy reconstitution; disclosed read-across; species/packaging controls)

Pb.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

Cd.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

tAs.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

iAs.rationale: Dairy regulations set total-arsenic limits, not a separate inorganic-arsenic limit. Total arsenic is measured on every lot and bounds the iAs fraction; an elevated total-As result triggers arsenic speciation.
iAs.reference_method: Total As by ICP-MS; iAs by HPLC-ICP-MS (EN 16802 or equivalent) on an elevated total-As result.

tHg.basis_note: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (face value)
tHg.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

MeHg.rationale: There is no methylmercury bioaccumulation pathway in dairy and no sovereign dairy MeHg maximum. Total mercury is measured on every lot and bounds the methylmercury fraction.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS; reflex MeHg speciation only if total Hg approaches the category ceiling.

Ni.basis_note: nearest sovereign value, face value (disclosed read-across; no government ML for this product form)
Ni.rationale: Conservative sovereign dairy read-across from the EU liquid infant/young-child formula nickel maximum (100 ug/kg) where no general-dairy nickel maximum exists.

Sn.rationale: Tin is a packaging-migration analyte. Non-tinplate dairy products have no intrinsic tin pathway; products in tin-coated containers instead use the directly applicable canned/tin-coated dairy limit.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging declaration plus total Sn by ICP-MS; route tin-coated packs to the canned/tin-coated limit.

Al.basis_note: nearest sovereign value, face value (disclosed read-across; no government ML for this product form)
Al.rationale: Conservative sovereign dairy read-across from the AU-NZ non-soy infant-formula aluminium maximum (500 ug/kg); no general-dairy aluminium maximum is loaded.

Cr.basis_note: nearest sovereign value, face value (disclosed read-across; no government ML for this product form)
Cr.rationale: China GB 2762 total-chromium maximum for liquid milk (300 ug/kg), directly applicable to liquid/fermented milk and used as a disclosed dairy-matrix read-across for other non-powder dairy products.

Cr-VI.rationale: Total chromium is measured on every lot. Any total-Cr result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by EPA 3060A with IC-ICP-MS / EN 15192 or equivalent.

standards.name: Bone broth
standards.methodology_version: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; COMPOSITE — disclosed read-across from strictest applicable principal-component sovereign ML; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.rationale: the muscle-meat lead ML binds at 100 ug/kg, and four credible rows converge on that figure (FSANZ meat 100; Cap. 132V meat of cattle, pig, goat and sheep 100; Cap. 132V meat of poultry 100; Cap. 132V edible offal of poultry 100). The lead-accumulating-tissue analog is a LADDER of 100 to 500 across jurisdictions, not the single 500 figure v1.1 disclosed, and its strictest rung equals the adopted binding

Cd.rationale: cadmium also accumulates in bone; three credible rows converge at 50 ug/kg for animal muscle meat (EU 2023/915, Cap. 132V meat of cattle/pigs/goat/sheep, Cap. 132V meat of poultry) and the EU row binds by jurisdiction priority

tAs.rationale: Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets total arsenic at 500 ug/kg for meat of animal, meat of poultry, edible offal of animal and edible offal of poultry; all four converge on 500, meat of animal is the nearest applicable commodity, and the cell publishes 500 by disclosed read-across. v1.2 replaces a control whose stated reason was false

iAs.reference_method: Bounded by the published total-arsenic ceiling of 500 ug/kg (tAs cell, Cap. 132V read-across). REFLEX TRIGGER: inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS on any lot whose total arsenic reaches or approaches the tAs ceiling, on any lot whose total arsenic is materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation, and on any fish-bone broth regardless of total arsenic. v1.2 replaces v1.1's 'no reflex iAs speciation for terrestrial bone broth', which combined with a tAs cell that published no number left the speciation bound circular and numerically vacuous.

tHg.rationale: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets total mercury at 50 ug/kg for meat of animal, meat of poultry, edible offal of animal and edible offal of poultry; all four converge on 50 and meat of animal is the nearest applicable commodity, so it binds bone broth's mercury cell by disclosed read-across. Terrestrial animal meat and bone are not a mercury-bioaccumulation matrix, but a sovereign meat ML exists, so the cell is a disclosed read-across rather than a bare screen. A fish-derived bone broth additionally inherits the Category 6 seafood mercury ceiling; the stricter applicable value binds. Value and binding row unchanged from v1.1; v1.2 completes the ladder and states the Note 1 read-across ruling explicitly

MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the published total-mercury ceiling of 50 ug/kg (tHg cell). REFLEX TRIGGER: methylmercury speciation by species-specific isotope dilution GC-ICP-MS on any lot whose total mercury approaches the published total-mercury ceiling, and on any fish-bone broth regardless of total mercury.
